How Much Space Does a Small Utility Room Need?

Less than you might think: a kitchen designer quoted by Ideal Home says a utility can fit into as little as 0.36 m² if you build upwards, about the footprint of one 60 cm machine with a second stacked on top, while the average utility room is about 2.5 to 5 m². Use these sizes as a starting point:

  • One wall of units: about 1.5 to 1.8 m of wall for the machines and a sink or worktop, plus about 1 m of clear floor in front so you can open the doors and load comfortably (Heritage Build Group).
  • Stacked machines: a column about 60 cm wide and at least 170 cm tall, because each machine is roughly 85 cm high before you add the stacking kit (Bosch).
  • A washer dryer only: one 60 cm space under a worktop, the smallest option if there is no room for two machines.

Long, Narrow Utility Rooms

In a corridor-shaped utility, put the machines, sink and tall cupboard on one wall and keep the opposite side for shallow storage, such as slim open shelves or wall cupboards, so the walkway stays clear. Heritage Build Group suggests units on both walls only when the room is about 2 m wide. In anything narrower, open doors and drawers clash in the middle.

How much does it cost to build a utility room?

A refresh can cost a few hundred pounds: paint from about £100 and new units from £200. MyBuilder puts a small utility room conversion at about £10,000 to £15,000 and a utility room extension at £7,500 to £25,000. Moving water, waste or power adds the most to the bill.

What usually goes in a utility room?

A washing machine and tumble dryer, or a washer dryer, a sink, a worktop for folding and a tall cupboard for the mop, broom, vacuum and ironing board. Most also have shelves for detergents and an airer for drying, and some house a spare fridge or freezer.

What is a bootility room?

A bootility is a utility room that doubles as a boot room, usually by the back door. It combines the washing machine and sink with a bench, coat hooks, boot storage and a hard-wearing floor, so muddy kit and laundry are dealt with in one place before they reach the rest of the house.

What is the smallest size for a utility room?

A kitchen designer quoted by Ideal Home has fitted working utilities into as little as 0.36 m² by building upwards, about the footprint of one 60 cm machine. A single run of units is easier to use: allow about 1.5 to 1.8 m of wall and about 1 m of clear floor in front.
